course.title: Running and Cardio
course.tagline: Go from first run to 5K with a plan that builds stamina safely.

days.title: Your first run: walk and jog
days.goal: Start running the safe way: mix walking and slow jogging.

video.title: Couch to 5K (The Simple Plan That Actually Works)

steps: Walk fast for 5 minutes to warm up.
Jog slowly for 1 minute, then walk for 2 minutes.
Repeat 5 times.
Walk slowly for 5 minutes to cool down.
days.task: Do 5 rounds of 1 minute jog, 2 minutes walk.
days.challenge: Jog for 2 minutes in one round.

quiz.q: What is the best way to start running?
quiz.explain: Short jogs with walks build stamina safely.

quiz.q: How should your first jog feel?
options: Easy enough to talk while moving
quiz.explain: You should be able to talk during an easy jog.

quiz.q: What should you do at the end?
quiz.explain: A slow walk cools the body down gently.

days.title: Good running shoes
days.goal: Learn what makes a good running shoe and how it should fit.
steps: Wear shoes with soft soles and good grip.
Check the fit: a thumb's width between your longest toe and the shoe end.
Tie your laces snug, not tight.
Run in your shoes for 5 minutes and check for pain.
days.task: Check your shoe fit with the thumb test.
days.challenge: Walk and jog in your shoes and note any pain.

quiz.q: How should running shoes fit?
options: A thumb's width past your longest toe
quiz.explain: A thumb's width stops toes hitting the front.

quiz.q: What should the sole do?
options: Cushion your steps and grip the ground
quiz.explain: A soft, grippy sole protects your feet.

quiz.q: What should you do if shoes hurt?
options: Stop and try a different pair
quiz.explain: Painful shoes can cause injury.

days.title: How to breathe while running
days.goal: Learn slow, steady breathing for running.
steps: Breathe in through your nose and out through your mouth.
Try a rhythm: in for 3 steps, out for 3 steps.
Slow down if you cannot talk.
Practise the rhythm on your next walk-jog.
days.task: Practise in-for-3, out-for-3 breathing on a walk.
days.challenge: Run one round breathing only through your nose.

quiz.q: How should you breathe while running?
options: Slow and steady, in nose, out mouth
quiz.explain: Slow breathing keeps you calm and steady.

quiz.q: What is a good breathing rhythm?
options: In for 3 steps, out for 3 steps
In for 1 step, out for 1 step
quiz.explain: A steady rhythm keeps breathing calm.

quiz.q: What should you do if you cannot talk while running?
quiz.explain: Slowing down brings breathing back to calm.

days.title: Run tall: good form
days.goal: Learn simple running form: tall body, relaxed arms.
steps: Stand tall and look forward, not down.
Keep your shoulders relaxed and down.
Swing your arms forward and back, not across your body.
Land softly on the middle of your foot.
days.task: Run for 5 minutes focusing on tall posture.
days.challenge: Ask a friend to watch your arms while you run.

quiz.q: Where should you look while running?
options: Forward, not down at your feet
quiz.explain: Looking forward keeps your body tall.

quiz.q: What should your arms do?
quiz.explain: Arms swinging forward and back help you run.

quiz.q: How should your feet land?
options: Softly on the middle of the foot
quiz.explain: A soft landing protects your joints.

days.title: Walk fast to build stamina
days.goal: Build your base with fast walking.
steps: Walk fast for 20 minutes today.
Swing your arms as you walk.
Keep a pace where you breathe faster but can still talk.
Write down how far you walked.
days.task: Walk fast for 20 minutes today.
days.challenge: Walk fast for 30 minutes tomorrow.

quiz.q: What is stamina?
options: How long you can keep going without getting tired
quiz.explain: Stamina is lasting power.

quiz.q: Why walk fast before running more?
quiz.explain: Fast walking builds stamina without strain.

quiz.q: How should fast walking feel?
options: Breathing faster but still able to talk
quiz.explain: You should be warm but able to talk.

days.title: Your first 2 km
days.goal: Run and walk your first 2 kilometres.

video.title: Low-Impact Aerobics Workout AND What Is Cardio?

steps: Warm up with a 5-minute fast walk.
Jog 2 minutes, walk 1 minute, repeat until you reach 2 km.
Cool down with a 5-minute slow walk.
Write down your time.
days.task: Cover 2 km with jog and walk rounds.
days.challenge: Jog 3 minutes in one round.

quiz.q: How should you reach 2 km first?
quiz.explain: Jog-walk rounds get you there safely.

quiz.q: What should you do if you get tired?
options: Walk until you feel ready, then jog again
quiz.explain: Walking breaks let you finish the distance.

quiz.q: Why write down your time?
options: So you can see yourself getting faster
quiz.explain: Your time shows progress.

days.title: PROJECT WEEK 1: Your walk-jog plan
days.goal: Put week 1 together: write your own walk-jog plan.

video.title: 14 BASIC STEP AEROBICS MOVEMENTS FOR BEGINNERS

steps: Write 3 sessions for next week: walk-jog rounds.
Each session: warm-up, jog-walk rounds, cool-down.
Make each session a little longer than the last.
Do session 1 and write your time.
days.task: Write your 3-session plan and do session 1.
days.challenge: Do all 3 sessions this week.

quiz.q: What should each session have?
quiz.explain: A full session warms up, works and cools down.

quiz.q: How should sessions change through the week?
quiz.explain: Small adds build stamina safely.

quiz.q: Why write your plan down?
options: So you can follow it and see progress
quiz.explain: A written plan is easy to follow.

project.title: Your walk-jog plan
project.brief: Write your own walk-jog plan with 3 sessions, warm-up, jog-walk rounds and cool-down, and do session 1.

days.title: Rest and stretch for runners
days.goal: Learn stretches that keep runners healthy.

video.title: Do This 10 Min Slow Jog Workout at Home (Standing, Low Impact, No Jumping)

steps: Stretch your calves: step back, press the heel down, hold 20 seconds.
Stretch your thighs: hold your foot behind you, hold 20 seconds.
Stretch your hips: low lunge, hold 20 seconds per side.
Take a rest day today.
days.task: Do the 3 stretches after your next run.
days.challenge: Hold each stretch for 30 seconds.

quiz.q: Why stretch after running?
options: It makes you faster at once
quiz.explain: Stretching after a run eases stiffness.

quiz.q: How long should you hold a stretch?
quiz.explain: Twenty seconds lets the muscle relax.

quiz.q: What is a good rest-day activity?
options: A slow walk or gentle stretch
quiz.explain: Gentle movement helps recovery.

days.title: Run 5 minutes without stopping
days.goal: Build up to 5 minutes of steady jogging.
steps: Warm up with a 5-minute walk.
Jog slowly for 5 minutes without stopping.
If you need to, walk for 1 minute and try again.
Cool down with a slow walk.
days.task: Jog for 5 minutes without stopping.
days.challenge: Jog for 6 minutes without stopping.

quiz.q: How do you run longer?
options: Slow down and build up a little at a time
quiz.explain: Slow and steady builds distance.

quiz.q: What should you do if you must stop?
quiz.explain: A walk break is part of learning.

quiz.q: How fast should a steady jog be?
quiz.explain: Talking pace is the right pace.

days.title: Step aerobics for cardio
days.goal: Learn simple step moves for cardio at home.

video.title: Beginner Total Body Strength Training for Runners

steps: Learn the basic step: up, up, down, down on a low step.
Try a knee lift on the step.
Try a side step on and off the step.
Do each move for 1 minute.
days.task: Do 5 minutes of step moves.
days.challenge: Add arm swings to your step moves.

quiz.q: What is step aerobics?
options: Cardio moves on and off a low step
quiz.explain: Step aerobics uses a low platform for cardio.

quiz.q: How high should your step be?
quiz.explain: A low step is safe for beginners.

quiz.q: What should you do if you lose the rhythm?
options: Slow down and march in place
quiz.explain: Slowing down gets your rhythm back.

days.title: Interval training, simply
days.goal: Learn intervals: short faster bits with easy bits in between.
steps: Walk fast for 2 minutes, then jog for 1 minute.
Repeat 5 times.
Cool down with a slow walk.
Write down how you felt.
days.task: Do 5 rounds of 2 minutes fast walk, 1 minute jog.
days.challenge: Try 1 minute fast, 2 minutes easy, 5 times.

quiz.q: What is interval training?
options: Short faster bits with easy bits in between
quiz.explain: Intervals mix effort and rest.

quiz.q: Why use intervals?
options: They build speed and stamina faster
quiz.explain: Intervals train the heart in short bursts.

quiz.q: How should the fast bit feel?
quiz.explain: Hard but doable is the right effort.

days.title: Run on different ground
days.goal: Learn how running feels on grass, road and track.
steps: Run on grass today: it is softer on your legs.
Run on a road tomorrow: watch for cars and holes.
Try a track if you can: flat and safe.
Write down which ground felt best.
days.task: Run on grass today.
days.challenge: Try a new route this week.

quiz.q: Why is grass good for beginners?
options: It is soft on the legs
quiz.explain: Soft ground lowers impact on joints.

quiz.q: What should you watch for on roads?
quiz.explain: Roads need care for safety.

quiz.q: Why try different routes?
options: It keeps running fun and fresh
quiz.explain: New routes keep you motivated.

days.title: Strength for runners
days.goal: Learn 3 strength moves that help runners.
steps: Do 10 squats, 10 lunges and a 20-second plank.
Rest 1 minute and repeat once.
Do this 2 times this week.
Write down your numbers.
days.task: Do 2 rounds of squats, lunges and plank.
days.challenge: Add 2 reps to each move next time.

quiz.q: Why do runners need strength?
options: Strong legs prevent injury and help you run better
quiz.explain: Strength protects joints and improves running.

quiz.q: What is a good runner strength move?
quiz.explain: Squats build the legs runners need.

quiz.q: How often should runners do strength?
quiz.explain: Twice a week is enough to help.

days.title: PROJECT WEEK 2: Your 3 km plan
days.goal: Put week 2 together: build a plan to reach 3 km.

video.title: Couch to 5K (The Simple Plan That Actually Works)

steps: Write 3 sessions: jog-walk rounds that reach 3 km.
Make the jog parts a little longer each session.
Do session 1 and write your time.
Rest one day between sessions.
days.task: Write your 3 km plan and do session 1.
days.challenge: Reach 3 km by the end of the week.

quiz.q: What is the goal this week?
quiz.explain: Three kilometres is a safe next step.

quiz.q: How should the jog parts change?
quiz.explain: Small adds build stamina safely.

quiz.q: Why rest between sessions?
options: Rest lets the body repair and get stronger
quiz.explain: Rest days are when the body gets stronger.

project.title: Your 3 km plan
project.brief: Build a plan to reach 3 km with jog-walk rounds, longer jog parts each session, and rest days between sessions.
checks: Reached 3 km by the end of the week

days.title: Run 10 minutes without stopping
days.goal: Build up to 10 minutes of steady running.
steps: Warm up with a 5-minute walk.
Jog slowly for 10 minutes.
Walk if you must, then jog again.
Cool down with a slow walk and stretch.
days.task: Jog for 10 minutes without stopping.
days.challenge: Jog for 12 minutes without stopping.

quiz.q: How do you reach 10 minutes?
options: Build up a little at a time
quiz.explain: Small adds each week build distance.

quiz.q: What should you do if you need a break?
options: Walk for 1 minute, then jog again
quiz.explain: A short walk break is part of training.

quiz.q: How should a 10-minute jog feel?
quiz.explain: Steady and talkable is the right pace.

days.title: Eat and drink for running
days.goal: Learn simple food and water rules for runners.
steps: Eat a light meal 2 hours before a run.
Drink water before, during and after long runs.
Eat carbs before a run for energy.
Eat protein after a run to repair muscles.
days.task: Drink water before and after your run today.
days.challenge: Eat a banana 1 hour before your run.

quiz.q: When should you eat before a run?
options: A light meal about 2 hours before
quiz.explain: Two hours gives time to digest.

quiz.q: What should you eat before a run?
options: Carbs for energy, like a banana
quiz.explain: Carbs give energy for the run.

quiz.q: Why drink water while running?
quiz.explain: Water replaces sweat and keeps you strong.

days.title: Run in the morning
days.goal: Learn how to run well in the morning.
steps: Wake up, drink a glass of water.
Eat a small snack like a banana.
Warm up with a 5-minute walk.
Run your session and stretch after.
days.task: Run in the morning tomorrow.
days.challenge: Run in the morning 3 times this week.

quiz.q: Why drink water first in the morning?
options: It is a rule with no reason
You wake up a little dry
quiz.explain: Water after sleep wakes the body up.

quiz.q: What is a good pre-run snack?
quiz.explain: A banana gives quick energy.

quiz.q: How long should you warm up?
quiz.explain: Five minutes wakes the body up.

days.title: Deal with a side stitch
days.goal: Learn what a side stitch is and how to fix it.
steps: A side stitch is a sharp pain under your ribs while running.
Slow down to a walk and breathe slowly.
Press gently on the sore spot while breathing out.
Do not eat a big meal right before running.
days.task: Practise slow breathing on your next run.
days.challenge: Walk for 2 minutes if a stitch comes.

quiz.q: What is a side stitch?
options: A sharp pain under the ribs while running
quiz.explain: A stitch is a common, harmless pain.

quiz.q: What should you do if you get one?
options: Slow to a walk and breathe slowly
quiz.explain: Slowing down and breathing eases a stitch.

quiz.q: How can you avoid a stitch?
options: Do not eat a big meal right before running
quiz.explain: A light stomach helps prevent stitches.

days.title: Run with a friend
days.goal: Run with a friend to make it fun and steady.

video.title: Low-Impact Aerobics Workout AND What Is Cardio?

steps: Invite a friend to run with you.
Run at a pace where you can both talk.
Take turns leading the pace.
Write down how the run felt.
days.task: Run with a friend this week.
days.challenge: Run at talking pace for 15 minutes with a friend.

quiz.q: Why run with a friend?
options: It makes running fun and keeps you going
quiz.explain: A friend adds fun and keeps you honest.

quiz.q: What pace should you run with a friend?
quiz.explain: Talking pace lets you both enjoy the run.

quiz.q: What should you do if your friend is faster?
options: Try to keep up and get hurt
Run your own pace and meet at the end
quiz.explain: Your own pace keeps you safe.

days.title: Your first 5K plan
days.goal: Learn the plan that takes you from running to 5K.

video.title: 14 BASIC STEP AEROBICS MOVEMENTS FOR BEGINNERS

steps: A 5K is 5 kilometres.
Build up: add 5 minutes to your long run each week.
Run 3 times a week: 2 short runs and 1 long run.
Write your 4-week 5K plan.
days.task: Write your 4-week 5K plan.
days.challenge: Add 5 minutes to your long run this week.

quiz.q: How far is a 5K?
quiz.explain: A 5K is 5 kilometres.

quiz.q: How should you build to 5K?
options: Add a little distance each week
quiz.explain: Small weekly adds build you to 5K safely.

quiz.q: How many runs a week suit a beginner?
quiz.explain: Three runs give growth and rest.

days.title: PROJECT WEEK 3: Your 5K plan
days.goal: Put week 3 together: start your 4-week 5K plan.

video.title: Do This 10 Min Slow Jog Workout at Home (Standing, Low Impact, No Jumping)

steps: Write your plan: 3 runs a week for 4 weeks.
Week 1: run 15 minutes, jog-walk as needed.
Add 5 minutes to the long run each week.
Do week 1, session 1 today.
days.task: Write your 5K plan and start week 1.
days.challenge: Finish all 3 runs in week 1.

quiz.q: How many weeks does the plan take?
quiz.explain: Four weeks builds you to 5K safely.

quiz.q: What should each week add?
options: A little more time or distance
quiz.explain: Small adds keep progress safe.

quiz.q: What should you do if you miss a run?
options: Do it the next day or move on
quiz.explain: One missed run does not ruin the plan.

project.title: Your 5K plan
project.brief: Write a 4-week 5K plan with 3 runs a week, 2 short runs and 1 long run, adding 5 minutes to the long run each week.
checks: Long run grows 5 minutes a week

days.title: Run 20 minutes without stopping
days.goal: Build up to 20 minutes of steady running.
steps: Warm up with a 5-minute walk.
Jog slowly for 20 minutes.
Walk for 1 minute if you must, then jog again.
Cool down and stretch.
days.task: Jog for 20 minutes without stopping.
days.challenge: Jog for 25 minutes without stopping.

quiz.q: How do you reach 20 minutes?
options: Add a few minutes each week
quiz.explain: Small weekly adds build distance.

quiz.q: What should you do if you feel very tired?
options: Slow down or walk for a minute
quiz.explain: Slowing down keeps you safe.

quiz.q: What is a good pace for a long run?
quiz.explain: Slow and talkable builds stamina.

days.title: Warm up and cool down well
days.goal: Learn a full warm-up and cool-down for runners.

video.title: Beginner Total Body Strength Training for Runners

steps: Warm-up: 5-minute walk, leg swings, gentle jog.
Cool-down: 5-minute slow walk, calf and thigh stretches.
Do both every time you run.
Write the steps on a card.
days.task: Do the full warm-up and cool-down today.
days.challenge: Teach the warm-up to a friend.

quiz.q: What should a warm-up include?
options: Walking, leg swings and a gentle jog
quiz.explain: A warm-up wakes the body up slowly.

quiz.q: What should a cool-down include?
quiz.explain: A cool-down slows the body down gently.

quiz.q: Why warm up and cool down every time?
quiz.explain: Warm-ups and cool-downs protect the body.

days.title: Race day: your first fun run
days.goal: Learn how to enjoy your first 5K fun run.
steps: Pick a local fun run and sign up.
Run your plan in the weeks before.
On race day, start slow and enjoy it.
Celebrate at the finish, whatever your time.
days.task: Find a local fun run to aim for.
days.challenge: Tell a friend about your race goal.

quiz.q: How should you start a race?
quiz.explain: Starting slow saves energy for the finish.

quiz.q: What should you do the week before a race?
quiz.explain: An easy week leaves you fresh for race day.

quiz.q: What matters most on race day?
quiz.explain: Finishing your first race is the win.

days.title: Keep running for life
days.goal: Learn how to keep running as a habit.
steps: Run 3 times a week, even if short.
Join a local running group.
Set a new goal: a longer run or a faster time.
Write down why you love running.
days.task: Join or find a running group this week.
days.challenge: Set your next running goal.

quiz.q: How often should you run to keep the habit?
quiz.explain: Three times a week keeps the habit alive.

quiz.q: Why join a running group?
quiz.explain: A group adds fun and keeps you honest.

quiz.q: What is a good next goal?
options: A longer run or a faster time
quiz.explain: A new goal keeps you growing.

days.title: Run your first 3 km
days.goal: Run 3 km without stopping for long.
steps: Warm up with a 5-minute walk.
Run slowly and steadily.
If you need to stop, walk for 1 minute, then run again.
Breathe in through your nose and out through your mouth.
Finish with a 5-minute walk.
Stretch your legs after.
days.task: Run 3 km today; walking breaks are fine.
days.challenge: Run the whole 3 km with only 1 walking break.

quiz.q: What should you do if you need to stop?
options: Walk for 1 minute, then run again
quiz.explain: A short walk lets you recover and keep going.

quiz.q: Why run slowly at first?
options: So you can keep going longer
quiz.explain: A slow pace saves energy for the whole run.

quiz.q: What should you do after the run?
options: Stop at once and sit down
quiz.explain: A cool-down walk and stretch help you recover.

days.title: Train your core for running
days.goal: Learn 3 core moves that help runners.

video.title: Couch to 5K (The Simple Plan That Actually Works)

steps: Plank for 20 seconds.
Side plank for 15 seconds on each side.
Dead bug 10 times: lie on your back, arms up, legs up, lower one arm and the other leg slowly.
Breathe out as you tighten your belly.
Rest 30 seconds between moves.
Do 2 rounds.
days.task: Do the 3 core moves today.
days.challenge: Hold the plank for 30 seconds.

quiz.q: Why do runners need a strong core?
options: It makes you faster at once
It keeps your body steady as you run
quiz.explain: A steady core keeps your running form clean.

quiz.q: How long should you hold a plank to start?
quiz.explain: Twenty seconds is a good start for a beginner.

quiz.q: What should you do with your breath in a plank?
quiz.explain: Slow steady breathing keeps the core working safely.

days.title: Get ready for your capstone
days.goal: Review the whole course and prepare your final run.
steps: Read your notes from weeks 1 to 4.
List 5 things you learned about running.
Practise your capstone run once.
Write down any questions you still have.
days.task: List 5 things you learned in this course.
days.challenge: Run your capstone distance from memory.

quiz.q: What is the capstone?
options: A final run that shows what you learned
quiz.explain: The capstone is your final show of skill.

quiz.q: What should you review before the capstone?
options: Your notes from all four weeks
quiz.explain: Reviewing all weeks brings the course together.

quiz.q: How do you know you are ready?
options: You can run your distance steadily and safely
quiz.explain: A steady, safe run shows you are ready.

days.title: Final practice day
days.goal: Practise your capstone run once more, then rest.
steps: Run your capstone distance one more time.
Check your pace: slow and talkable.
Fix anything that felt hard.
Rest well tonight.
days.task: Run your capstone distance and time it.
days.challenge: Fix one hard part of your run.

quiz.q: Why practise once more?
options: Practice makes the real run calm and smooth
quiz.explain: Practice turns worry into calm confidence.

quiz.q: What should you check after practice?
options: Your pace, your breathing and your form
quiz.explain: Checking pace and breathing makes the run smooth.

quiz.q: What should you do the night before?
quiz.explain: Good rest helps you run your best.

days.title: Capstone day: run your 5K
days.goal: Show what you learned: run 5 kilometres.
steps: Warm up with a 5-minute walk.
Run 5 km at a steady, talkable pace.
Walk for 1 minute if you must, then run again.
Cool down, stretch and write your report.
days.task: Run your 5K and write your report.
days.challenge: Hand in your report and celebrate.

quiz.q: How far is your capstone run?
quiz.explain: The capstone is a 5K run.

quiz.q: What pace should you run?
quiz.explain: A steady pace gets you to the finish.

quiz.q: What goes in your report?
options: Your time, your pace and how you felt
quiz.explain: A short report shows what you learned.

capstone.title: Run your first 5K
capstone.brief: Run 5 kilometres at a steady, talkable pace, with a warm-up and cool-down, and write a short report on your time, pace and how you felt.
deliverables: A list of your run times
A short video or notes from the run
